description: Complete single-player tactical mech combat game with voice-first accessibility, AI tactician, mission generator, and progression system
gameFlow: TITLE SCREEN -> NEW PILOT or CONTINUE -> PILOT QUARTERS (hub) -> MISSION SELECT -> MISSION BRIEFING -> COMBAT -> MISSION DEBRIEF -> PROGRESSION -> back to PILOT QUARTERS

epics.name: Core Game Flow
epics.description: Title screen, hub navigation, mission flow screens

epics.name: AI Tactician
epics.description: LLM-powered opponent that reasons about tactics and executes valid combat actions

epics.name: Voice Interface
epics.description: Speech-to-text input, voice intent parsing, text-to-speech feedback

epics.name: Mission Generator
epics.description: Procedural mission creation with LLM-generated narrative

epics.name: Accessibility Polish
epics.description: Canvas accessibility, screen reader support, reduced motion, keyboard shortcuts

epics.name: Combat Polish

epics.name: Game Flow Safety
epics.description: Mid-mission controls, pause functionality, auto-save, progress protection

userStories.title: Title Screen
userStories.description: Replace current dashboard with game title screen featuring New Pilot/Continue/Quick Battle/Settings buttons. This is the entry point for the entire game.
acceptanceCriteria: Route `/` renders title screen instead of current dashboard
Displays game title 'LANCER TACTICS AI' and tagline
Four buttons: New Pilot, Continue, Quick Battle, Settings
Continue button disabled if no saved pilot exists
Quick Battle launches combat with preset pilot/mech (for testing)
All buttons keyboard accessible (Tab navigation, Enter to activate)
ARIA labels on all interactive elements
`make test-app` passes
userStories.notes: Implemented title screen with game title, tagline, four buttons. Continue button disabled when no saved pilot exists (checks via API). Quick Battle uses existing demo combat. All buttons have ARIA labels and keyboard navigation. Header hidden on title screen.

userStories.title: Pilot Quarters Hub
userStories.description: Central hub screen showing pilot/mech summary with navigation to missions, loadout, and compendium. This is the main menu after completing pilot creation.
acceptanceCriteria: Route `/quarters` renders hub screen
Displays current pilot name, license level, and mech frame
Navigation buttons: Pilot, Mech, Missions, Compendium
Shows mission count badge on Missions button
Prominent 'Deploy to Mission' button (disabled if no mission selected)
Keyboard navigation between all buttons
Redirects to title if no active pilot
`make test-app` passes
userStories.notes: Implemented quarters hub at /quarters with pilot/mech summary using active character (first character). Navigation buttons with keyboard arrow key support. Mission count badge placeholder (3). Deploy button disabled pending mission selection. Redirects to title if no saved pilot. All acceptance criteria satisfied.

Arrow key navigation between mission cards

userStories.notes: Implemented mission select screen at /missions with static mission data, lock icons based on pilot license level, arrow key navigation, and placeholder briefing route. All acceptance criteria satisfied.

userStories.title: Combat State Serializer
userStories.description: Create a serializer that converts MechCombatScenario state into a structured, LLM-readable format with all information needed for tactical decisions.
acceptanceCriteria: Function `serialize_combat_state(scenario: MechCombatScenario) -> dict` in `llm/src/tactician/state_serializer.py`
Output includes: current actor, all combatants (position, HP, heat, conditions), available actions for current actor
Output includes: terrain/hazards on the map, turn order, round number
Positions use hex coordinates matching the combat grid
Actions include their parameters (targets, ranges, damage predictions)
Unit tests in `llm/tests/tactician/test_state_serializer.py` covering various combat states
`make test-llm` passes
userStories.notes: Implemented serialize_combat_state() with: current actor detection via get_current_actor; combatant serialization with hex positions, stats, resources; terrain serialization extracting tiles with properties (dangerous, cover, etc.); turn order with side and acted status; action parameters including potential targets (enemies within sensor range) with distances, damage predictions based on actor's first usable weapon (min/max/average). All acceptance criteria satisfied. Unit tests pass.

userStories.title: Tactical System Prompt
userStories.description: Design the system prompt that instructs the LLM how to reason about Lancer tactics by NPC role (striker, defender, artillery, etc).
acceptanceCriteria: System prompt template in `llm/src/tactician/prompts/tactical_system.md`
Prompt explains Lancer combat basics (heat, structure, conditions)
Prompt defines output format: JSON with action type, target, reasoning
Includes few-shot examples of good tactical reasoning
Role-specific tactics: striker (aggressive), defender (protect allies), artillery (range)
Prompt template function in `llm/src/tactician/prompts.py` that fills in combat state
Documentation of prompt design decisions in `llm/src/tactician/README.md`
userStories.notes: Created tactical system prompt with Lancer combat basics, role-specific tactics, few-shot examples, and prompt template functions. All files placed in llm/src/tactician/ with proper documentation.

userStories.title: Action Parser and Validator
userStories.description: Parse LLM output into validated combat actions that can be executed by the combat system.
acceptanceCriteria: Function `parse_llm_action(llm_output: str, available_actions: list) -> Action` in `llm/src/tactician/action_parser.py`
Handles JSON parsing with fallback for malformed output
Validates parsed action against available_actions list
Returns closest valid action if exact match fails (fuzzy matching)
Raises clear error if no valid action can be determined
Unit tests covering: valid JSON, malformed JSON, invalid action, fuzzy matching
`make test-llm` passes
userStories.notes: Implemented parse_llm_action function with JSON extraction, validation, fuzzy matching, and unit tests. All acceptance criteria satisfied.

userStories.title: Tactician Integration

Method `decide_action(scenario: MechCombatScenario, actor_id: str) -> Action`
